lines: –Approximately $33.1 million of contracted proceeds outstanding with approximately $9.6 million expected to be received during the remainder of fiscal 2027

desk.headline: Revenue up 26% to $2.0m, just below estimate; loss of $0.25 a share narrower than expected; no guidance
results: Spectrum lease revenue rose 26% to $2.0m, slightly under the $2.0m estimate.
The company lost $5.0m ($0.25 a share), against a $53.5m profit a year ago that was lifted by large one-off gains on spectrum licence swaps and sales.
This quarter's licence-swap gain was only $6.1m, while operating costs rose 15% to $13.8m.
Cash was $107.5m with no debt; $33.1m of contracted payments is still to come, $9.6m of it this fiscal year.
No shares were bought back; the full $250m buyback programme remains unused.

guidance.summary: Anterix gives no revenue or earnings guidance. It only says about $9.6m of contracted payments should arrive in the rest of fiscal 2027.

points: The pipeline of active spectrum deals grew to 16 from about 12 last quarter, with at least half said to be well advanced.
No new utility contracts were signed for a second quarter in a row.
Management pointed to a recent big 800 MHz spectrum sale at a higher price per MHz-pop than its own average, and is pushing buyers to pay more.
About 85% of its 900 MHz spectrum is still available; buyers now include satellite and direct-to-phone players, depending on an FCC rule change proposed on 29 Oct.
Liquidity comes first, which is why no shares were bought back.
call.source: Call coverage — Earnings Whispers via Finviz, 11 Nov 2026; Quartr call summary; The Motley Fool, 11 Nov 2026

watch: Whether any of the 16 pipeline deals turn into signed contracts.
The outcome of the FCC proposal to add 900 MHz to satellite-to-phone bands.
Use of the $250m buyback and the cash burn from spectrum clearing.
